strengths: Disciplined separation of primary evidence, selected numerical checks, positive controls, and unpooled context.
Concrete phase-aware lifecycle contract for immutable shared and private mutable state.
Named memory denominators and bounded claims.
issues: Producer-captured digest evidence lacks an independent producer recapture.
Per-call compiled binary and autotuning provenance remain unbound.
One sequential Qwen/H20 setting leaves concurrent and cross-stack generality open.
Context cohorts and caveats remain dense.

strengths: Concrete ownership protocol and useful internal controls.
Clear separation of relational, numerical, fault, and allocator evidence.
issues: The PDF-only snapshot did not expose the artifact package, so this reviewer could not execute the named replay paths.
Selected operator checks and partial dispatch binding leave common-mode paths open.
The sequential single-stack setting does not establish realistic concurrent serving.
Exact selection metadata for the oracle rows is not compactly visible in the PDF.

strengths: Coherent phase-aware receipt contract and honest limitations.
Meaningful four-cell design, numerical checks, and targeted positive controls.
Nine-page main paper includes reproducibility and ethics statements.
issues: Candidate-emitted receipt capture and partial dispatch provenance cap assurance.
One model, sequential schedule, one main geometry, and selected operator rows cap generality.
The dense appendix and artifact map increase reader burden.

review_access_caveat: All reviewers were intentionally restricted to the PDF-only snapshot. The research artifact exists outside that snapshot; inability to execute it under this access mode is not evidence that it is absent, but the PDF must still describe the release boundary clearly.
